scope_notes: Snapshot Git attributes disable text conversion to preserve inventory hashes on every platform.
Snapshot ignore rules expose only the fourteen explicitly allowed native bin assets.
Only 13 graph-related source skills and all four graph production Python runtimes are included.
Foundry IQ and entity skills/runtimes are excluded; graph-router references to them describe external routes.
Skills and runtime packages remain in separate top-level directories; all runtime and native assets retain their existing paths.
Evaluation routes, scripts and supporting guides are omitted.
GRZ fixture backend, native fixture generator, full-generation test reader and developer simulator are omitted.
GRZ Azure build/read paths and native output conversion are retained.
Explicit GRZ CLI native-binary now reaches the build runner; source/env overrides precede distribution locations.
Runtime development/test dependencies, test configuration, EKG sample fixture data and internal contribution records are omitted.
Ordinary operations use domain CLIs without MCP; EKG and GRZ register optional Apps adapters, and ontology's optional Apps adapter requires an explicit absolute state directory.
Skill/plugin versions are provisional snapshots, not assured or published releases.
Python dependency manifests retain updated exact upstream production pins and optional Apps extras; no transitive lockfile or wheelhouse is shipped.
Azure MCP @latest remains an external, unpinned dependency.
Five native platform builds come from user-supplied archives, not the pinned Python source; byte-identical vendor references are shared at the bin root.
All shipped native checksums and OS/CPU headers are verified; only Windows x64 was live-tested. Windows Authenticode status is NotSigned.
Local and wheel resolution selects the host RID after explicit/environment overrides; mismatched binary headers are rejected.
Unix executables may require chmod +x after installation; the runner verifies checksums before checking execute permission.
The user-supplied archive includes no third-party notice or standalone license file; this is not a signed customer release.
Native community labeling configuration requires AOAI URI/key-environment fields not supplied by the Python build adapter.
Native clustering reads the vector field from the approved source binding instead of assuming vector.
Accepted EKG, GRZ and ontology Apps HTML, notices and provenance are copied byte-for-byte from the pinned source, without line-ending normalization.
